text:
jane-customer: Hey team — customers started hitting 502/504s from the hosted API ~09:10 UTC. Mostly /v1/generate. Seen ~15% error rate on requests. Any known incidents? :rotating_light:
ashley: Thanks — can you paste a failing request id or curl repro? Also which region?
jane-customer: region=us-west-2, example request id header: x-request-id=rcw-9a3b2. Quick repro curl: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-base\",\"input\":\"test\"}'` -> 502.
oncall-bot: [alert] memcached-prefix-cluster-us-west-2 increased connection errors: 09:08 -> 09:14 UTC, 6xx -> 60xx/sec. Latency p95 climbed from 8ms -> 120ms.
ashley: @devon can you check prefix cache / memcached pool? Sounds like dependency timeouts cascading to gateway.
devon: Looking. I can already see a spike in `connect_timeouts` and `evictions` on memcached-prefix-usw2. Metrics: connections open peaked at 60k (pool cap 48k), auth failures ~0. No config changes in last 24h. Likely pool saturation + eviction storms.
sasha: If memcached is slow, gateway requests waiting on prefix KV will hit our upstream timeout and return 502/504. We should bypass prefix cache for hosted API traffic while we stabilize.
ashley: Agreed. Two actions: 1) temporary gateway config to bypass prefix cache for the hosted API route; 2) scale memcached prefix cluster and restart the most affected nodes. I'll coordinate.
ashley: @devon can you run the bypass toggle? Provide the command or console link so I can patch customer-facing docs.
devon: Patching route config now — setting `prefix_cache.enabled=false` on route `hosted-api-us-west-2` via console. Will take effect in ~30s. Also opening a memcached scale job to add 4 read replicas.
devon: Patch applied. Host gateway logs show immediate drop in prefix cache calls. Error rate dropping from 15% -> 3% in the last 2 mins.
jane-customer: Confirming — my requests are succeeding now. Thanks.
ashley: For repro and for engineering: here's a short repro that simulates the failure surface (spams many small requests that hit prefix lookup):
```
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "X-Request-ID: repro-$i" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-base","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
Run from multiple clients to recreate connection pressure.
devon: Additional root-cause evidence in memcached logs: repeated `IOERR: accept() resource temporarily unavailable` and `connection queue overflow`. Also saw a config on the gateway side with an aggressive `max_pool_per_route` leading to more sockets than cache nodes could handle.
infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-2042. Linked: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-2042
sasha: Temporary mitigations we took: 1) bypass prefix cache for hosted route; 2) scaled memcached cluster + restarted 3 nodes; 3) adjusted gateway connection pool defaults to limit per-worker sockets; 4) enabled short-circuit fallback to origin (skip KV on prefix miss) for heavy routes.
ashley: Customer impact summary for support notes: immediate error spike 09:08–09:16 UTC, peaked ~18% 502/504s. After bypass at 09:17, errors dropped to <2%.
jane-customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround — do you plan a permanent fix?
sasha: Next steps: full postmortem, add autoscaling on prefix cluster based on connection queue depth, increase pool size conservatively, and add graceful degrade mode when KV latency > 50ms (auto-bypass). Also add a canary for gateway pool changes.
devon: I'll also add improved alerting thresholds: connection_queue_depth and eviction_rate alerts should fire earlier.
ashley: Action items assigned:
- devon: scale tuning + alerts (ETA 3h)
- sasha: GRACEFUL_BYPASS feature design + canary (ETA 1d)
- infra: postmortem writeup and customer RCA (ETA 2d)
- support (ashley): follow up with impacted customers + update status page (now + follow-up)

ashley: Closing thread for live mitigation. Please add follow-ups to INC-2026-2042 and PRs to the repo. :thumbsup:
